record.title: Acute kidney injury in a dog successfully treated with hemodialysis: a case report
record.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) in dogs represents a significant clinical challenge, particularly when conservative therapy fails to restore renal function. This case report describes the management and favourable outcome of a German Shorthaired Pointer that had previously been diagnosed and treated for babesiosis, which subsequently developed severe azotemia and biochemical alterations consistent with AKI, successfully managed with hemodialysis. The patient was referred with lethargy, anorexia, vomiting, and laboratory findings indicative of renal dysfunction, including elevated serum creatinine, urea, and phosphorus concentrations, along with mild hypoalbuminemia and hypoproteinemia. Urine output was preserved, but azotemia persisted despite appropriate fluid therapy, electrolyte correction, and supportive care. Hemodialysis was initiated as renal replacement therapy using a standard extracorporeal circuit under continuous monitoring. Treatment resulted in progressive improvement of biochemical parameters and clinical condition, with complete normalisation of renal function shortly after the final dialysis session. The patient was discharged in good clinical condition and maintained stable renal values during follow-up. This case highlights the clinical applicability and effectiveness of hemodialysis as a therapeutic option in canine AKI unresponsive to medical treatment. Early recognition of candidates for renal replacement therapy and prompt initiation of hemodialysis can significantly improve prognosis and clinical outcomes in dogs with acute kidney injury.

screening.rationale: AKI case managed with haemodialysis after treated babesiosis. Full text must show whether the AKI is attributed to babesiosis (a renal complication).
